evidence.summary: Kpler preliminary data: four commodity-vessel transits Thursday, three inbound and one outbound, down from six Wednesday and below the 10-day average near 16. AIS-off traffic remains an explicit undercount limitation. Three LNG vessels reappeared outside Hormuz, including Qatar-loaded Al Daayen and Al Samriya; Kpler also records a Sep. 13 dark STS transfer between Al Rayyan and Al Mashabiyyah off Oman. Bab el-Mandeb recorded 23 commodity transits versus a 10-day average near 26.
unresolved: Whether LNG movements represent sustained reopening or episodic extraction

evidence.summary: Reuters satellite analysis plus three industry sources independently confirm damage at three pumping stations serving the Saudi East-West Pipeline, one more than previously assessed. The 1,200-km pipeline temporarily shut; repair estimates vary, with three sources saying five to six weeks and another allowing earlier partial pumping. The system has 11 pumping stations plus two pressure-relief stations and had been moving roughly 4-5 mb/d. This strengthens and refines the prior Kpler multi-station BDA: station damage is confirmed, not destruction of the pipeline body.
supersedes_or_updates: Saudi East-West Pipeline / Yanbu BDA drawer

evidence.summary: Brent remained above $100, trading about $104.49 by 1411 GMT while WTI was about $102.79. Reuters reports Bloomberg's claim that Aramco told at least two European refining customers they would receive no October crude following the East-West Pipeline attack; preserve the customer-allocation report as secondary until Aramco/customer confirmation.
unresolved: Aramco confirmation of October European allocation cuts

evidence.summary: Iranian state media now names the Togo-flagged tanker as Trend and attributes the statement to IRGC Navy commander Rear Adm. Ali Azmaei. IRGC says Trend was struck, caught fire and stopped after attempting an unauthorized passage allegedly at U.S. military direction. This updates vessel identity only at claimant-source level; weapon, casualties, independent fire/damage confirmation and U.S. involvement remain unverified.

Reuters reports aid agencies saying about 115,000 people are on the move after the Houthi advance. AP separately reports OCHA estimates about 125,000 have fled homes, eight civilians killed and 32 wounded in latest fighting, while Yemen government health authorities attribute roughly 150 civilian deaths since Sep. 3 to Houthis. Preserve these as distinct source/denominator series rather than overwriting the earlier IOM DTM 104,796 IDP baseline.
unresolved: Independent attribution audit of government-reported civilian deaths

evidence.summary: AP independently reports Oman hosted a meeting last weekend between U.S. and Houthi representatives, citing a Houthi official and another person familiar with the talks. Houthis publicly frame their present targeting as Saudi shipping; U.S. says it is in constant contact with Riyadh. Preserve the contact as confirmed multi-source diplomacy, but public evidence still does not establish a formal U.S.-Houthi nonaggression agreement or its exact terms.
unresolved: Whether Saudi attacks/shipping were discussed as a condition

evidence.summary: Reuters reports Iran will be on the agenda for the Sep. 24 Trump-Xi summit. Washington views Xi as potentially able to pressure Tehran; Treasury Secretary Bessent is also due to discuss China's financial ties to Tehran with Vice Premier He Lifeng. Reuters notes Treasury has so far stopped short of penalties on Chinese banks in the current economic campaign. This extends the China-pressure drawer but is not evidence of a Chinese commitment to coerce Iran.
supersedes_or_updates: Operation Economic Outcast / China exposure drawer
unresolved: Whether Washington seeks concrete Chinese banking/oil measures
